structured_output.summary:
Kitchen module (parts/room-12.mjs) is written: east-wall range (smoker, furnace, cauldron sink, barrel) on a smooth_stone counter, a central island, a sink counter under the south windows, 3 standing and 2 chained hanging lanterns, candles and flower pots. Verified alone in a scratch grid: room check OK, walk 130/130, min light 7, 1 dim cell, fit OK, and the scratch render reads as a kitchen.
Not in the full build: shell.mjs:27 fills every interior cell with air and runParts locks it, so all 31 kitchen writes are REFUSED. make.sh still writes a whole build.nbt. The shell has to stop filling interiors with air; this is noted in plan.md's Notes.

waste.what: Drew the kitchen floor grid by hand from the plan output, then placed each furniture row and light by counting character indices in the y4/y5/y8/y9 layers.
waste.cost: about 6 layer rewrites; one row off-by-one fixed by hand; ~40 minutes of thinking-free editing was avoided only by reusing the layers() grid
waste.tool: a room-furnish helper that takes a named furniture list (item, face, position relative to a wall or counter) and returns the layers() grid, auto-placing standing or hanging lanterns to clear the dark cells the room check names

waste.what: Found the air-lock refusal only at make.sh time: the room check on the full build showed 0 placed and 31 refused, with no earlier warning that the shell had locked the interior.
waste.cost: one full make.sh run plus a scratch harness (scratch.mjs and a rooms file with the entrance moved inside the box) to test the module alone
waste.tool: runParts should report the earlier part and the cell that locked each room's box before a room part runs, and mcd room should accept --entrance so one room can be checked in a fresh grid without the whole build

waste.what: Light tuning by trial: hanging lanterns at y8 under a chain light only radius 2-3 at floor level, so I moved to standing lanterns on the counter and island and added floor lanterns, one rebuild per try.
waste.tool: mcd light with a per-height table (what radius a hanging lantern at y8 or y9 lights at feet level) would have chosen the lantern heights up front
